# std/net.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from std/net.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

TCP sockets for programs on the hosted target (Linux and
the other targets whose native or C backend links the C library's socket
calls). Built on the `Host` capability, so a kernel or user program that
imports this file is rejected (`E-TARGET`). A call that fails (no such
listener, a closed descriptor, an address in use) gives `Option::None` or
`false`. On Windows the calls go to Winsock, loaded on the first call.

`import "std/net.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`net_ip4`](#net_ip4) | An IPv4 address from its four parts, as `host_net` takes it. |
| [`net_listen`](#net_listen) | Starts listening on `ip`:`port` (port 0 picks a free one). |
| [`net_port`](#net_port) | The port a listening socket is bound to. |
| [`net_connect`](#net_connect) | Connects to `ip`:`port`. |
| [`net_accept`](#net_accept) | Waits for a connection on a listening socket and returns it. |
| [`net_recv`](#net_recv) | Reads up to `max` bytes into `out` (replacing it). |
| [`net_send_all`](#net_send_all) | Sends all of `data`, retrying after a partial write. |
| [`net_close`](#net_close) | Closes a socket. |
| [`net_now`](#net_now) | The time in seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC, from the system clock (0 if there is none). |
| [`net_random`](#net_random) | `n` random bytes (at most 256) from the system's source (`/dev/urandom`, `RtlGenRandom`, `crypto.getRandomValues`), or `None` when there is none. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `net_ip4`

```bastio
fn net_ip4(a: u64, b: u64, c: u64, d: u64) -> u64
```

An IPv4 address from its four parts, as `host_net` takes it.

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
if lo != 2130706433 { return 1; }
```

### `net_listen`

```bastio
fn net_listen(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Starts listening on `ip`:`port` (port 0 picks a free one).

Example:

```bastio
match net_listen(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => { net_close(host, s); },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `net_port`

```bastio
fn net_port(h: &Host, sock: u64) -> u64
```

The port a listening socket is bound to.

Example:

```bastio
match net_listen(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    net_close(host, s);
    if p == 0 { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `net_connect`

```bastio
fn net_connect(h: &Host, ip: u64, port: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Connects to `ip`:`port`.

Example:

```bastio
// Nothing listens on port 1.
match net_connect(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 1) {
  Option::Some(s) => { net_close(host, s); return 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
```

### `net_accept`

```bastio
fn net_accept(h: &Host, sock: u64) -> Option[u64]
```

Waits for a connection on a listening socket and returns it.

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, s) {
          Option::Some(a) => { bad = 0; net_close(host, a); },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `net_recv`

```bastio
fn net_recv(h: &Host, sock: u64, max: u64, out: &mut Bytes) -> Option[u64]
```

Reads up to `max` bytes into `out` (replacing it). `Some(0)` is the end of
the stream.

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
let mut bad = 1;
match net_listen(host, lo, 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => {
    let p = net_port(host, s);
    match net_connect(host, lo, p) {
      Option::Some(c) => {
        match net_accept(host, s) {
          Option::Some(a) => {
            let msg = bfrom("hello");
            let sent = net_send_all(host, c, msg);
            bfree(msg);
            let mut got = balloc(0);
            match net_recv(host, a, 16, &mut got) {
              Option::Some(n) => { if sent && n == 5 { bad = 0; } },
              Option::None => {},
            }
            bfree(got);
            net_close(host, a);
          },
          Option::None => {},
        }
        net_close(host, c);
      },
      Option::None => {},
    }
    net_close(host, s);
  },
  Option::None => {},
}
if bad != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `net_send_all`

```bastio
fn net_send_all(h: &Host, sock: u64, data: &Bytes) -> bool
```

Sends all of `data`, retrying after a partial write. False if the
connection fails first.

Example:

```bastio
let lo = net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1);
match net_connect(host, lo, 1) {
  Option::Some(c) => { net_close(host, c); return 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
```

### `net_close`

```bastio
fn net_close(h: &Host, sock: u64)
```

Closes a socket.

Example:

```bastio
match net_listen(host, net_ip4(127, 0, 0, 1), 0) {
  Option::Some(s) => { net_close(host, s); },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `net_now`

```bastio
fn net_now(h: &Host) -> u64
```

The time in seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC, from the system clock (0 if
there is none). The caller of the TLS client gives this as `now`.

Example:

```bastio
// After 2023, and the clock does not run backwards.
let a = net_now(host);
let b = net_now(host);
if a < 1700000000 || b < a { return 1; }
```

### `net_random`

```bastio
fn net_random(h: &Host, n: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == n
```

`n` random bytes (at most 256) from the system's source (`/dev/urandom`,
`RtlGenRandom`, `crypto.getRandomValues`), or `None` when there is none.
The Bytes returned has exactly `n` bytes.

Example:

```bastio
match net_random(host, 32) {
  Option::Some(a) => {
    match net_random(host, 32) {
      Option::Some(b) => {
        // Two draws of 256 bits are the same with probability 2^-256.
        let same = bytes_eq(a, b);
        bfree(b);
        bfree(a);
        if same { return 1; }
      },
      Option::None => { bfree(a); return 1; },
    }
  },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```
